title: Me levanto
goal: Describe your daily routine from waking up to going to bed, using reflexive verbs.

lessons.title: Getting up
lessons.notes:
Some Spanish verbs come with **se** on the end of the infinitive: **levantarse** (to get up), **ducharse** (to have a shower). They're **reflexive**: you do the action to yourself - literally "to raise oneself".
The **se** moves to the front and changes with the person:
**yo me** levanto · **tú te** levantas · **él / ella / usted se** levanta · **nosotros nos** levantamos · **ellos / ustedes se** levantan
The verb itself is a normal -ar verb. You already know one: **me llamo** (I call myself) comes from **llamarse**.
**despertarse** (to wake up) also changes e -> ie, like querer: **me despierto**.

items.note: e -> ie: me despierto, te despiertas.

sentences.es: Me levanto a las seis y media.
sentences.en: I get up at half past six.
accept_en: I get up at six thirty.

sentences.es: ¿A qué hora te levantas?
sentences.en: What time do you get up?

sentences.es: Mi hermana se levanta muy temprano.
sentences.en: My sister gets up very early.

sentences.es: Los sábados nos levantamos tarde.
sentences.en: On Saturdays we get up late.

sentences.es: Me despierto con el despertador.
sentences.en: I wake up with the alarm clock.
accept_en: I wake up with the alarm.
I wake up to the alarm clock.
I wake up to the alarm.

sentences.es: Carlos se ducha por la mañana.
sentences.en: Carlos has a shower in the morning.
accept_en: Carlos takes a shower in the morning.

sentences.es: ¿Te duchas por la noche?
sentences.en: Do you have a shower at night?
accept_en: Do you take a shower at night?
Do you shower in the evening?

sentences.es: Mis padres se despiertan a las cinco.
sentences.en: My parents wake up at five.

lessons.title: Getting ready
lessons.notes:
More reflexive verbs for getting ready. With body parts, Spanish uses **el / la / los**, not "my": the **me** already says whose they are.
**Me lavo las manos.** = I wash my hands.
**Se cepilla los dientes.** = He brushes his teeth.
**vestirse** (to get dressed) changes e -> i: **me visto, te vistes, se viste, nos vestimos, se visten**.
Without **se**, the same verbs act on someone or something else: **lavo el carro** (I wash the car), **me lavo** (I wash myself).

items.note: e -> i: me visto, te vistes.
la mano is feminine although it ends in -o.
False friend: it doesn't mean large (that's grande).

sentences.es: Me lavo la cara con agua fría.
sentences.en: I wash my face with cold water.

sentences.es: Los niños se cepillan los dientes.
sentences.en: The children brush their teeth.

sentences.es: Mi papá se afeita todos los días.
sentences.en: My dad shaves every day.

sentences.es: Me visto rápido porque es tarde.
sentences.en: I get dressed quickly because it's late.
accept_en: I get dressed fast because it's late.

sentences.es: ¿Te lavas las manos y la cara?
sentences.en: Do you wash your hands and face?
accept_en: Do you wash your hands and your face?

sentences.es: Ana se peina el pelo largo.
sentences.en: Ana combs her long hair.

sentences.es: Nos vestimos y desayunamos.
sentences.en: We get dressed and have breakfast.

sentences.es: Mi hermano se ducha muy rápido.
sentences.en: My brother has a very quick shower.
accept_en: My brother has a shower very quickly.

lessons.title: First, then, finally
lessons.notes:
To tell your routine in order, use these linking words:
**primero** (first) · **luego / después** (then, afterwards) · **por último** (finally)
**antes de** and **después de** take an **infinitive** - the -ar / -er / -ir form - where English uses -ing:
**después de comer** = after eating
With a reflexive verb the pronoun goes on the end and changes with the person: **antes de acostarme** (before I go to bed), **después de ducharte** (after you shower).
**acostarse** (to go to bed) changes o -> ue: **me acuesto**. So does **dormirse** (to fall asleep): **me duermo**.

items.note: o -> ue: me acuesto, te acuestas.
ponerse la ropa = to put your clothes on. Yo: me pongo.

sentences.es: Primero me ducho, luego me visto.
sentences.en: First I shower, then I get dressed.
accept_en: First I have a shower, then I get dressed.

sentences.es: Me acuesto a las once.
sentences.en: I go to bed at eleven.

sentences.es: ¿A qué hora te acuestas?
sentences.en: What time do you go to bed?

sentences.es: Leo un libro antes de dormirme.
sentences.en: I read a book before falling asleep.
accept_en: I read a book before I fall asleep.
I read a book before going to sleep.

sentences.es: Después de cenar, mi familia mira la televisión.
sentences.en: After dinner, my family watches television.
accept_en: After having dinner, my family watches TV.
After dinner, my family watches TV.

sentences.es: Me lavo los dientes después de desayunar.
sentences.en: I brush my teeth after breakfast.
accept_en: I brush my teeth after having breakfast.
I clean my teeth after breakfast.

sentences.es: Por último, me acuesto y leo.
sentences.en: Finally, I go to bed and read.
accept_en: Lastly, I go to bed and read.

sentences.es: Los niños se duermen muy rápido.
sentences.en: The children fall asleep very quickly.

sentences.es: Trabajo y luego voy al parque.
sentences.en: I work and then I go to the park.

sentences.es: Después de ducharme, me seco con la toalla.
sentences.en: After showering, I dry myself with the towel.
accept_en: After my shower, I dry myself with the towel.
After I shower, I dry off with the towel.

sentences.es: Me pongo el reloj antes de salir.
sentences.en: I put my watch on before going out.
accept_en: I put on my watch before I go out.
I put my watch on before leaving.

sentences.es: Por la noche me quito el reloj.
sentences.en: At night I take my watch off.
accept_en: I take off my watch at night.
In the evening I take my watch off.

lessons.title: Weekends and feelings
lessons.notes:
Many feelings and changes are reflexive in Spanish:
**divertirse** (to have fun) · **aburrirse** (to get bored) · **sentirse** (to feel) · **quedarse** (to stay) · **irse** (to leave, go away)
**divertirse** and **sentirse** change e -> ie: **me divierto, me siento**.
With **ir a**, **querer** or **poder** + infinitive, the pronoun can go in front or on the end - both are right:
**Me voy a quedar en casa.** = **Voy a quedarme en casa.**
**¿Te quieres ir?** = **¿Quieres irte?**
Careful: **me siento** is also "I sit down" (sentarse). Context makes it clear.

sentences.es: Los domingos me quedo en casa.
sentences.en: On Sundays I stay at home.

sentences.es: Nos divertimos mucho en la playa.
sentences.en: We have a lot of fun at the beach.
accept_en: We have lots of fun at the beach.
We have a great time at the beach.

sentences.es: ¿Te aburres en el trabajo?
sentences.en: Do you get bored at work?

sentences.es: Hoy no me siento bien.
sentences.en: I don't feel well today.

sentences.es: Es tarde, me voy.
sentences.en: It's late, I'm leaving.

sentences.es: Voy a quedarme en casa el sábado.
sentences.en: I'm going to stay at home on Saturday.
accept: Me voy a quedar en casa el sábado.
accept_en: I'm going to stay home on Saturday.

sentences.es: Quiero relajarme el fin de semana.
sentences.en: I want to relax on the weekend.
accept_en: I want to relax at the weekend.

sentences.es: Mis amigos se van a las diez.
sentences.en: My friends leave at ten.
accept_en: My friends are leaving at ten.

sentences.es: Los niños nunca se aburren en el parque.
sentences.en: The children never get bored at the park.
accept_en: The kids never get bored in the park.
The children never get bored in the park.
